questions:
1. **Which of the three proposed options ships?** The issue offers: an Italic option in the panel, Ctrl+I / Cmd+I, or an italic font. *Suggested:* an "Italic" toggle in the properties panel **and** Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on macOS); no separate italic font in the font list.
2. **Scope of italic: whole element or part of the text?** *Suggested:* italic is one property of the whole text element; there is no partial italic (no rich text).
3. **Toggle placement, label and tooltip.** *Suggested:* an "Italic" toggle next to the text align control, tooltip "Italic (Ctrl+I)"; shown when a text, a shape with text or an arrow with a label is selected, or the Text tool is active.
4. **Ctrl+I behavior.** *Suggested:* toggles italic on the selected text and on the text being edited (even if only part of it is highlighted it applies to the whole element); with nothing selected it does nothing; the browser's own Ctrl+I action (e.g. Firefox "Page Info") never opens while the canvas has focus.
5. **Fonts without a real italic face** (e.g. Hand-drawn/Excalifont, Code/Comic Shanns, fonts in the full list, CJK fallback). *Suggested:* every font can be italic; where the font has no italic face, the text is slanted (synthetic oblique). The toggle is never disabled.
6. **Several texts selected, only some italic.** *Suggested:* toggle shows as not pressed; one click makes all italic, a second click makes all upright.
7. **Default for new text.** *Suggested:* the last chosen italic value becomes the default for new text, like font family and size.
8. **Layout.** *Suggested:* the slanted last character is never clipped; the text box widens to fit; text inside a shape re-wraps to the shape width (shape grows taller, width unchanged); an arrow label stays at the middle of the arrow; a sticky note's auto-fit takes italic into account.
9. **Persistence and sharing.** *Suggested:* italic survives page reload, saved .excalidraw file, PNG and SVG export (including SVG on a computer without the fonts), copy as PNG/SVG, and live collaboration; an older Excalidraw version opens a file with italic text without error and shows it upright.
10. **Copies, styles and history.** *Suggested:* paste styles, Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V, Ctrl+D, Alt+drag and library items carry italic; one toggle is undone with a single undo.
11. **Scripts.** *Suggested:* right-to-left (Arabic, Hebrew), CJK and emoji render without clipping and without breaking line layout; emoji may look upright (browser decides) — no specific slant required for them.
12. **Platforms.** *Suggested:* current desktop Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge on Windows and macOS, plus the mobile layout (375 px wide) where the toggle must be reachable; no locale-specific label work beyond fallback to English.
13. **Combination with underline** (issue 99001, not released). *Suggested:* out of scope for these cases; add a combination case once underline ships.
answers:
1. (user) A panel toggle and Ctrl/Cmd+I; one italic property per text element, no separate italic font.
2. (user) Italic applies to the whole text element only; there is no partial italic. Bold is out of scope.
3. (accepted suggestion) An "Italic" toggle next to the text align control, tooltip "Italic (Ctrl+I)"; shown when a text, a shape with text or an arrow with a label is selected, or the Text tool is active.
4. (accepted suggestion) Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on macOS) toggles italic on the selected text and on the text being edited (even if only part of it is highlighted, it applies to the whole element); with nothing selected it does nothing; the browser's own Ctrl+I action (e.g. Firefox "Page Info") never opens while the canvas has focus.
5. (user) Synthetic oblique is allowed for fonts without an italic face; the text stays readable and unclipped. (accepted suggestion) Every font can be italic; the toggle is never disabled.
6. (accepted suggestion) With several texts selected and only some italic, the toggle shows as not pressed; one click makes all italic, a second click makes all upright.
7. (user) The last italic value becomes the default for new text.
8. (accepted suggestion) The slanted last character is never clipped; the text box widens to fit; text inside a shape re-wraps to the shape width (shape grows taller, width unchanged); an arrow label stays at the middle of the arrow; a sticky note's auto-fit takes italic into account.
9. (accepted suggestion) Italic survives page reload, a saved .excalidraw file, PNG and SVG export (including SVG opened on a computer without the fonts), copy as PNG/SVG, and live collaboration; an older Excalidraw version opens a file with italic text without error and shows it upright.
10. (accepted suggestion) Paste styles, Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V, Ctrl+D, Alt+drag and library items carry italic; one italic toggle is undone with a single undo.
11. (user) Italic text stays readable and unclipped in Latin, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Hebrew (right to left), emoji and mixed scripts; text direction and alignment are unchanged. (accepted suggestion) Whether emoji look slanted is left to the browser.
12. (accepted suggestion) Platforms: current desktop Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge on Windows and macOS, plus the mobile layout (375 px wide) where the toggle must be reachable; in other locales the "Italic" label falls back to English, never empty or a raw key.
13. (accepted suggestion) The combination with underline (issue 99001, not released) is out of scope; add a combination case once underline ships.
14. (user) Color and opacity changes keep italic.
